newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-China sees futures exchange rationalisation.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-China sees futures exchange rationalisation.

text.p: Competition will drive the number of futures exchanges in China down to four or five from 15, Xiaoqiang Wu, chairman of the Beijing Commodity Exchange said on Tuesday.
Exchanges with more regional economic advantages in China would survive while others will be forced out of business, Xiaoqiang told the Asia-Pacific Commodity Markets conference here.
"In the end, four or five exchanges will survive this tough competition in China and the risk hedging function of futures markets will be brought into better play," he said.
Xiaoqiang did not give a timeframe for the reduction in the number of exchanges, but said at one time there were over 40 exchanges operating in China.
He also said financial futures products would play a more important role in China in the future.
Futures trading in China was not open to foreigners under current laws, although eventually this might change, he added.
